ordered_diagnoses: Breast cancer with cutaneous lymphatic invasion

s1.syndrome_frame: Postoperative skin lesion with erythema and nodules
salient_findings: Pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site of the right breast
Well-demarcated, warm, erythematous plaque over the right side of the anterior chest wall
Multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels
key_facts: History of right breast cancer, stage IIIa (cT2N2M0)
Underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by right modified radical mastectomy and postoperative radiotherapy
Lesion did not respond to initial topical treatments
Presentation to dermatology 1 year after initial cancer diagnosis
Multiple palpable small nodules within the erythema
Immunohistochemistry negative for ER, PR, and HER2
Skin biopsy showed multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels

shortlist.label: Cutaneous metastasis

shortlist.label: Carcinomatous lymphangitis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin biopsy showing multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels, indicating lymphatic invasion

shortlist.label: Breast cancer with cutaneous lymphatic invasion
shortlist.why_kept: History of breast cancer and clinical presentation consistent with cutaneous lymphatic invasion

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels on skin biopsy, along with the clinical presentation of a pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cutaneous metastasis
rejected.why: While possible, the specific involvement of lymphatic vessels suggests a more specific diagnosis related to lymphatic invasion.

rejected.label: Inflammatory breast carcinoma
rejected.why: This typically presents at the time of initial cancer diagnosis, not a year later, and the clinical description does not fully align with the characteristic diffuse erythema and edema of inflammatory breast cancer.

rejected.label: Lymphangitic carcinoma
rejected.why: This term, while related, is less specific and does not fully capture the clinical and pathological findings presented.

rejected.label: Breast cancer with cutaneous lymphatic invasion
rejected.why: This option is broader and does not specifically describe the clinical presentation and biopsy findings as accurately as carcinomatous lymphangitis.

gold: Carcinoma erysipelatoides arising from triple-negative breast cancer
